method: After freezing the decision and canonical pair, returned to Appendix 1 and Article 5.3 before reconsidering course support. Rebuilt the credit buckets and checked the bounded claims on the live prospectus, the adopted regulations and current UCR course evidence. Then checked the exact finished schedules and content selections.
findings: September 2026 entrants take 180 EC in English. Year one comprises 60 EC across Biomedical Expert (28), Investigator and Scholar (12), Communicator and Collaborator (10), Professional and Organizer (10). Year two has 43 fixed EC and three choice positions of 6, 6 and 5 EC, including metabolism or cell signalling, biorhythms or neuromuscular control, and systems biology, allometry or epigenomics. Year three has a 30 EC minor and 30 EC of required major study, including a single 22 EC bundle for internship, individual thesis and oral defence. An internal biomedical minor takes one 12 EC course in each of two periods and a shared 6 EC review unit. Other 30 EC study requires approval. The Dutch educational minor is listed at 40 EC and is not used in this 180 EC pathway.

Article 5.3 allows unconditional year-two entry at 60 EC and conditional at 43 EC with 31 biomedical/investigator, 6 professional and 6 communication EC and remediation. Unconditional year-three entry takes 120 EC. Conditional entry takes 60 from year one and 43 in the same competency distribution from year two, with remediation and regular examination dates. For internship and thesis, 20 communication, 20 professional and 20 investigator EC are required. The thesis is individual, with at least two assessors and an oral defence. The coordinator approves the internship and the Board appoints the supervisor. Attendance and participation are assessed within the existing competencies or courses. First-year advice is non-binding and no extra required credits are counted for the stated competency activities.

The EER identifies the 5 EC biomedical data science and machine-learning unit. UCR data handling plus predictive modelling and validation create real partial coverage in the research option, with medical examples in both the machine-learning and image-analysis content. Introductory data preparation precedes advanced modelling and imaging is offered in term six. The UCR lab course covers blood and molecular or microbial practicals, with separate anatomy observation and related data work. Maastricht’s assessed competencies, placement and thesis remain distinct. Product Design is offered in term one and supplies working mechanisms, fabrication and prototype practice. Later market and strategy work gives the enterprise option a different purpose while retaining all eleven biomedical courses. No research placement or clinical-business training is assumed.
